_meta.title: Push-surface ratchet ceilings (#1273)
_meta.description: Anti-regrowth ratchet on the always-pushed context layer. Each surface has two ceilings (items and bytes); the guard fails red when a surface exceeds either. CONTEXT.md as a whole file is deliberately NOT capped (see context_md_whole_file).
_meta.item_definition: An 'item' is a line whose stripped form is a bullet ('- ', '* ', or '+ ' at any nesting depth) or a numbered list line ('N. ' or 'N) '). Block-level HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) are excluded before counting. Fenced code, YAML frontmatter, and .claude/rules/* files without a paths: key are all COUNTED — they are pushed at session start. This definition is load-bearing and is asserted by a synthetic-fixture test in tests/ci/test_push_surface_guard.py.

margin.statement: Ceilings = per-surface 90-day maximum (git-history max over the last 90 days, computed at fixture-writing time 2026-07-31, except invariants_md/glossary_index_md which are new files created 2026-08-07 by #1417 — their ceiling is measured-at-creation + 20% margin) + 20% margin, rounded up. #1417 retired the SessionStart hook's budget-constrained CONTEXT.md push (context_md_pushed, dropped in 47% of sessions) in favor of two static files delivered via bare @import — invariants_md (30 items/5,359 bytes) and glossary_index_md (8 items/1,104 bytes) — which now carry their own ceilings under the same 20%-margin policy, no longer bounded by ASSEMBLY_BUDGET_CHARS.
margin.uuids: Each surface entry carries the record_decision UUID that set its ceiling (adjacent comment), per the Quota-Probe.ps1 precedent. Bumping a ceiling without a fresh record_decision UUID is a review failure.

provenance.source: Issue #1273 records aggregate 90-day maxima of 129 items / 49,632 bytes across the four source files. Per-surface ceilings here are computed from per-surface git-history maxima: soul_md 38/9512, project_claude_md 65/25283 (pre-#1252 compression), userlevel_claude_md 30/16498, userlevel_doctrine_md 9/6870 (file created 2026-07-30, max == current). #1417 (2026-08-07) replaced context_md_pushed with two @import-delivered files: invariants_md 30 items/5,359 bytes measured-at-creation, glossary_index_md 8 items/1,104 bytes measured-at-creation.
provenance.basis: post-compression sizes (#1265-#1268 closed); #1417 extraction for invariants_md/glossary_index_md

_meta.same_pr_raise: The JSON IS the fixture: the guard reads ceilings only from this file, so raising a ceiling is impossible without editing it in the same PR. Regrowth is therefore a reviewable act.

context_md_whole_file.note: CONTEXT.md as a whole file has NO ceiling — pull-only Glossary bodies may grow freely (that is the push/pull split). The formerly-pushed part (Invariants + Glossary category index) now lives in its own ratcheted files — see surfaces.invariants_md and surfaces.glossary_index_md — delivered via @import instead of the SessionStart hook assembler.

soul_md.note: Identity. Loaded via a bare `@SOUL.md` import in .claude-userlevel/CLAUDE.md, not a SessionStart hook step (#1328).

project_claude_md.note: Repo rules. Loaded by the harness into every jarvis session.

userlevel_claude_md.note: User-level CLAUDE.md source (installer source, not the repo-local mirror). Loaded into every session on every device.

userlevel_doctrine_md.note: Shared cross-repo norms, @import-ed from user-level CLAUDE.md.

invariants_md.note: Extracted ## Invariants, delivered via a bare @docs/context/invariants.md import in CLAUDE.md — replaces the SessionStart hook's context_md_pushed surface (#1417). Ceiling = measured-at-creation 30 items / 5,359 bytes + 20% margin, rounded up. Not bounded by ASSEMBLY_BUDGET_CHARS — @import bypasses the assembler entirely.

glossary_index_md.note: Extracted Glossary category+count index, delivered via a bare @docs/context/glossary-index.md import in CLAUDE.md — replaces the SessionStart hook's context_md_pushed surface (#1417). Ceiling = measured-at-creation 8 items / 1,104 bytes + 20% margin, rounded up. Not bounded by ASSEMBLY_BUDGET_CHARS — @import bypasses the assembler entirely.
